text:
Every member of the swimming club may use the town pool free of charge on Sundays. You are not a member of the club, so you cannot count on free entry to the pool on Sunday.
Which one of the following most closely parallels this reasoning?
options: Every airline pilot must pass a medical examination. You failed yours, so you cannot become a pilot.
All the students who passed the exam received a certificate. You received a certificate, so you passed.
Club members get free entry on Sundays. You are a member, so your entry this Sunday is free.
The only way into the final is to win the semi-final. Your team lost its semi-final, so it cannot play in the final.
Everyone who buys a season ticket gets free parking at the stadium. You have no season ticket, so you are not guaranteed free parking.
solution: The argument has the form: everyone in group G gets benefit B; you are not in G; so B is not GUARANTEED for you. The season-ticket option matches, including the careful conclusion (not guaranteed, rather than refused). The pilot and semi-final options are about a requirement that, if missing, rules something out completely; the certificate option reasons backwards; the third applies the rule to a member.

text:
In a survey, 15% of the students named biology as their favourite subject, 25% named chemistry and 35% named physics. Another 9 students liked all three equally, and the remaining 21 students liked none of them.
How many students took part in the survey?
solution: 15% + 25% + 35% = 75% chose one subject, so the other 25% is made up of the 9 + 21 = 30 remaining students. If 25% is 30 students, the whole survey is 4 x 30 = 120.

text:
Five red beads and fifteen white beads are threaded in some order on a closed loop of string. The beads are arranged so that as few white beads as possible have no red bead touching them.
How many white beads have no red bead touching them?
solution: Each red bead touches two neighbours, so at most 5 x 2 = 10 white beads can touch a red one, and that needs at least two white beads between every pair of red beads, so no white bead touches two reds. Then 10 white beads touch a red and 15 - 10 = 5 do not. It cannot be fewer, because 10 is the most places next to a red bead.

text:
Laura needs 30 party invitations, all of one design. She will only buy invitations printed on recycled paper.

| design | invitations per pack | recycled paper | price per pack |
|---|---|---|---|
| stars | 6 | yes | £1.50 |
| balloons | 10 | no | £2.00 |
| flowers | 8 | yes | £1.90 |
| animals | 12 | yes | £3.20 |
| rockets | 15 | yes | £4.10 |

What is the least she can spend?
solution: Balloons are not recycled, so they are out (3 packs for £6.00 is the trap). For 30 invitations: stars need 5 packs = £7.50; flowers need 4 packs (32) = £7.60; animals need 3 packs (36) = £9.60; rockets need 2 packs = £8.20. The cheapest is £7.50.

text:
A greengrocer paints a word in capital letters on a glass door, one letter under another down the door. She wants it to read correctly from inside the shop as well as from outside.
Which word would work?
solution: Seen from behind, each letter is mirrored left to right. Written vertically, the order of the letters stays the same, so the word works only if every letter is symmetrical about a vertical line. T, O, M and A all are. LEMON fails on L, E and N; BANANA on B and N; CHERRY on C, E and R; GRAPE on G, R, P and E.

text: Which pair of scholar and field of study is NOT correct?
solution: Johannes Kepler was an astronomer and mathematician, known for the laws of planetary motion, not a physician. Darwin developed evolution by natural selection, Lavoisier founded modern chemistry, Freud founded psychoanalysis, and Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations founded modern economics.

text: Who wrote the novel The Name of the Rose, a murder mystery set in a medieval monastery?
solution: Umberto Eco, the semiotician from Alessandria, published The Name of the Rose in 1980. Calvino wrote If on a Winter's Night a Traveller, Manzoni The Betrothed, Primo Levi If This Is a Man, and Elsa Morante History.

text: In UNESCO, the United Nations agency, what does the letter S stand for?
solution: UNESCO is the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. It works through education, science and culture, and keeps the list of World Heritage Sites.

text: Which museum is correctly paired with its city?
solution: The Uffizi Gallery is in Florence. The Prado is in Madrid, the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg, the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam and the Louvre in Paris.

text: Magna Carta, agreed by King John of England in 1215, is best known for
options: uniting the kingdoms of England and Scotland.
limiting the power of the king and protecting certain rights of his subjects.
solution: Magna Carta placed the king under the law, for example protecting free men from imprisonment without lawful judgement; it became a symbol of limited government. England and Scotland united in 1707, the Hundred Years' War ended in 1453, and Henry VIII broke with Rome in the 1530s.

text: Which institution of the European Union has the main right to propose new EU laws?
options: the Court of Justice of the European Union
solution: The European Commission proposes legislation (the right of initiative); the European Parliament and the Council of the EU then amend and adopt it. The European Council of heads of government sets overall direction but does not legislate, the Court interprets EU law, and the ECB runs monetary policy.

text: Which director made the films La Dolce Vita and 8½?
solution: Federico Fellini directed La Dolce Vita (1960) and 8½ (1963). Rossellini made Rome, Open City; De Sica made Bicycle Thieves; Antonioni made L'Avventura; Pasolini made The Gospel According to St Matthew.

text: Which pair of scientist and discovery is NOT correct?
options: Gregor Mendel: the laws of inheritance
Galileo Galilei: the structure of DNA
solution: The double helix of DNA was described by Watson and Crick in 1953, using Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images; Galileo, three centuries earlier, studied motion and observed the moons of Jupiter. The other pairs are correct.

text: Which treaty, signed in 1992, created the European Union and set the path towards the euro?
solution: The Treaty of Maastricht (1992, in force 1993) created the European Union and planned economic and monetary union. Paris (1951) founded the Coal and Steel Community, Rome (1957) the European Economic Community, Lisbon (2007) reformed the EU, and Westphalia (1648) ended the Thirty Years' War.

text: Which international organisation lends to member countries facing a balance-of-payments crisis and monitors the stability of the world economy?
solution: The International Monetary Fund (IMF), founded at Bretton Woods in 1944, gives short-term loans to countries that cannot pay their international bills and watches over the global financial system. The WTO handles trade rules, UNICEF children's welfare, the OECD economic policy research, and the WHO health.

text: Which pair of Italian author and work is NOT correct?
solution: The Leopard (Il Gattopardo) was written by Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa and published in 1958; Giacomo Leopardi was a 19th-century poet, best known for the Canti. The other four pairs are correct.

text: What does the principle of the "separation of powers" mean?
options: dividing the legislative, executive and judicial functions of the state between separate bodies
dividing a country into regions, each with its own parliament
keeping religion and the state apart
dividing parliament into two chambers with equal powers
requiring an election for every public office
solution: Associated with Montesquieu, the separation of powers gives law-making to parliament, government to the executive and judgement to independent courts, so that no single body holds all power. Regional parliaments are devolution or federalism, church and state apart is secularism, and two equal chambers is perfect bicameralism.

text:
Which of the following structures is/are present in a typical bacterial cell?
1 a cell wall
2 ribosomes
3 mitochondria
solution: Bacteria are prokaryotes. Most have a cell wall (made of peptidoglycan), and all have ribosomes, smaller (70S) than those of eukaryotes. They have no membrane-bound organelles, so no mitochondria: respiration happens on the cell membrane. So 1 and 2 only.

text:
Two molecules of glucose and one molecule of fructose, each \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\), are joined by condensation reactions to form a trisaccharide.
What is the molecular formula of the trisaccharide?
solution: Joining three monosaccharides makes two glycosidic bonds, and each condensation removes one water. Three \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) make \(\mathrm{C_{18}H_{36}O_{18}}\); taking away \(\mathrm{2H_2O}\) leaves \(\mathrm{C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}}\).

text: Which of the following is correct for the phospholipids in a cell membrane?
options: They are the main route by which ions cross the membrane.
Their hydrophilic heads face the inside of the bilayer.
Their hydrophobic fatty acid tails face the inside of the bilayer, away from water.
They are joined to one another by peptide bonds.
They are made in the nucleus.
solution: A phospholipid has a hydrophilic phosphate head and two hydrophobic fatty acid tails. In water they form a bilayer with the heads facing the watery inside and outside of the cell and the tails hidden in the middle. Ions cross through channel and carrier proteins, because the hydrophobic core blocks them; phospholipids are made on the smooth ER.

text:
Which of the following contain(s) enzymes?
1 saliva
2 lysosomes
3 the stroma of chloroplasts
solution: Saliva contains amylase. Lysosomes are bags of hydrolytic enzymes that digest worn-out organelles and engulfed material. The stroma holds the enzymes of the Calvin cycle, including rubisco. All three.

text: Which of the following processes involves a redox reaction?
options: hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and phosphate
formation of a peptide bond between two amino acids
osmosis of water into a root hair cell
conversion of pyruvate to lactate during fermentation
solution: In lactic acid fermentation NADH gives its hydrogen to pyruvate: pyruvate is reduced to lactate and NADH is oxidised back to \(\mathrm{NAD^+}\). Hydrolysis and condensation (peptide bond) involve no change in oxidation state, osmosis is the movement of water, and base pairing uses hydrogen bonds.

text:
In humans, a person with at least one Y chromosome normally develops as male, whatever the number of X chromosomes.
Using this information, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 A person with the sex chromosomes XXY normally develops as male.
2 A person with one X chromosome and no Y chromosome normally develops as male.
3 An XXY zygote could result from a normal egg being fertilised by a sperm that carries both an X and a Y chromosome.
solution: 1: XXY has a Y, so male (Klinefelter syndrome). 2: XO has no Y, so female (Turner syndrome). 3: if X and Y fail to separate in meiosis I, a sperm can carry both; with the egg's X this gives XXY. So 1 and 3 only.

text:
A cell containing three pairs of homologous chromosomes divides by mitosis, and then each daughter cell divides by mitosis again.
Which row shows the number of cells produced and the number of chromosomes in each?

| | number of cells produced | chromosomes in each cell |
|---|---|---|
| row 1 | 2 | 3 |
| row 2 | 4 | 6 |
| row 3 | 4 | 3 |
| row 4 | 4 | 12 |
| row 5 | 2 | 6 |
solution: Three pairs means 6 chromosomes. Mitosis makes two cells genetically identical to the parent, so each division keeps 6 chromosomes per cell. Two rounds give 4 cells, each with 6. Halving to 3 happens only in meiosis.

text: While the electron transport chain of a mitochondrion is working, where is the concentration of protons (hydrogen ions) highest?
solution: The electron transport chain uses the energy of electrons to pump protons from the matrix across the inner membrane into the intermembrane space. That builds the gradient that drives the protons back through ATP synthase. So the intermembrane space has the highest concentration and the matrix the lowest.

text:
Which row could be correct for stabilising selection?

| | the most common phenotype is favoured | the range of phenotypes becomes narrower | the mean value of the trait shifts |
|---|---|---|---|
| row 1 | ✓ | x | ✓ |
| row 2 | x | ✓ | ✓ |
| row 3 | x | x | ✓ |
| row 4 | ✓ | ✓ | x |
| row 5 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

Key: ✓ yes, x no
solution: Stabilising selection removes the extremes and favours the middle, most common phenotype. The spread of phenotypes narrows but the mean stays where it is. A shifting mean is the mark of directional selection. Row 4.

text: Which one of the following statements about the healthy human heart is correct?
options: The right ventricle has a thicker muscular wall than the left ventricle.
The pulmonary artery carries oxygenated blood.
The sinoatrial node is in the wall of the left ventricle.
The atria and the ventricles contract at the same moment.
Blood leaving the left ventricle enters the aorta.
solution: The left ventricle pumps into the aorta and round the whole body, which is why its wall is the thickest. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs. The sinoatrial node, the pacemaker, is in the wall of the right atrium. The atria contract first and the ventricles a fraction of a second later.

text:
A patient with blood group AB (Rhesus factor ignored) needs a transfusion of red blood cells.
Red cells of which ABO blood group(s) can the patient safely receive?
solution: Group AB plasma carries neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies, so nothing in the patient's blood will attack red cells carrying A or B antigens. AB is the universal recipient and can receive red cells of any ABO group. Group O is the universal donor, the opposite case.

text:
As Group I of the Periodic Table (Li to Cs) is descended, which of the following properties of the elements INCREASE?
1 atomic radius
2 reactivity with water
3 melting point
solution: Each step down adds a shell, so the atoms get bigger (1). The outer electron is further from the nucleus and better shielded, so it is lost more easily and reactivity with water rises (2). Metallic bonding weakens as the atoms grow, so melting points fall, from about 180 °C for lithium to 28 °C for caesium. So 1 and 2 only.

text:
Atoms of element Q have 20 neutrons and a mass number of 40. Q forms ions by losing two electrons.
Which is the ground-state electron arrangement of a Q ion?
solution: Protons = 40 - 20 = 20, so the element is calcium. The atom has 20 electrons, \(1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}4s^{2}\); the \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) ion loses the two 4s electrons, leaving 18: \(1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}\), the argon arrangement.

chapter: States of Matter and Gas Laws
text:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 Dissolving sugar in water lowers the temperature at which the water freezes.
2 Water boils at a lower temperature at the top of a high mountain than at sea level.
3 Cooling a gas from 50 °C to 20 °C increases the average speed of its molecules.
solution: 1: a dissolved solute lowers the freezing point (and raises the boiling point). 2: water boils when its vapour pressure equals the air pressure; on a mountain the air pressure is lower, so that happens at a lower temperature. 3: lower temperature means lower average kinetic energy, so the molecules slow down. So 1 and 2 only.

text: Which of the following equations represents the first ionisation energy of sodium?
solution: The first ionisation energy is the energy to remove one electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms, forming one mole of gaseous 1+ ions. It starts from Na(g), not the solid, and is defined per mole of atoms, so the 2Na equation is twice the value. Adding an electron is electron affinity.

text:
Solution P: 200 mL of hydrochloric acid, concentration 0.020 mol/L.
Solution Q: 100 mL of sulfuric acid, concentration 0.010 mol/L.
Treat both acids as fully dissociated. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 P and Q have the same hydrogen ion concentration.
2 P contains more moles of hydrogen ions than Q.
3 Both solutions have a pH of exactly 2 at 25 °C.
solution: Each \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) gives two \(\mathrm{H^+}\), so Q has \([\mathrm{H^+}] = 0.020\) mol/L, the same as P (1 correct). Moles: P has 0.200 x 0.020 = 0.0040 mol, Q has 0.100 x 0.020 = 0.0020 mol (2 correct). pH = \(-\log(0.020) \approx 1.7\), not 2 (3 wrong).

text: These compounds have similar molar masses. Which of them has the highest boiling point?
solution: Only propan-1-ol has an O-H group, so only its molecules hydrogen-bond to each other; that is the strongest intermolecular force here, and it boils at about 97 °C. Propanal and methoxyethane are polar but have no O-H (about 48 °C and 7 °C), chloroethane about 12 °C, and non-polar propane about -42 °C.

text:
A solution contains 5.0 g of glucose in 250 mL. 10 mL of it is diluted with water to exactly 100 mL in a volumetric flask, and the flask is shaken. Then 20 mL of the diluted solution is transferred to a beaker.
What is the concentration of glucose in the beaker, in g \(\mathrm{L^{-1}}\)?
solution: Start: 5.0 g in 0.250 L = 20 g/L. Diluting 10 mL to 100 mL divides the concentration by 10: 2.0 g/L. Pouring out 20 mL changes the amount taken, not the concentration, so the beaker holds 2.0 g/L.

text:
A compound has the formula \(\mathrm{Ca}_m\mathrm{X}_2\mathrm{O}_n\), where calcium has its usual oxidation state of +2 and oxygen of -2.
Which expression gives the oxidation state of element X?
solution: A neutral compound's oxidation states add up to zero: \(2m + 2x - 2n = 0\), so \(2x = 2n - 2m\) and \(x = n - m\). (Check with calcium sulfate written as \(\mathrm{Ca_2S_2O_8}\): \(m = 2\), \(n = 8\) gives +6 for S.)

text:
A sample of an oxide of copper contains 2.54 g of copper combined with 0.32 g of oxygen.
Which formula fits this compound?
[Relative atomic masses: Cu = 63.5; O = 16]
solution: Moles of Cu = 2.54/63.5 = 0.040; moles of O = 0.32/16 = 0.020. The ratio Cu : O is 2 : 1, so the formula is \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\), copper(I) oxide.

subject: Mathematics
text:
Which one of the following is a simplification of
\[\frac{x^2 - 9}{x^2 + x - 6}\]
solution: Factorise both: \(x^2 - 9 = (x-3)(x+3)\) and \(x^2 + x - 6 = (x+3)(x-2)\). Cancelling \(x + 3\) leaves \(\dfrac{x-3}{x-2}\). Cancelling the \(x^2\) terms, as in the last option, is not allowed: only common factors cancel.

subject: Mathematics
text:
Solve the inequality
\[\tfrac{1}{3}(3x - 1) - \tfrac{1}{4}(2x + 6) > x - 4\]
solution: The left side is \(x - \tfrac{1}{3} - \tfrac{x}{2} - \tfrac{3}{2} = \tfrac{x}{2} - \tfrac{11}{6}\). So \(\tfrac{x}{2} - \tfrac{11}{6} > x - 4\), giving \(-\tfrac{x}{2} > -\tfrac{13}{6}\). Multiplying by \(-2\) reverses the sign: \(x < \tfrac{13}{3}\).

subject: Physics
text:
A child sits 1.5 m from the centre of a playground roundabout that turns at a constant angular velocity of 2.0 rad/s.
Which row gives the child's speed and the magnitude of their acceleration?

| | speed (m/s) | acceleration (\(\text{m/s}^{2}\)) |
|---|---|---|
| row 1 | 3.0 | 0 |
| row 2 | 1.5 | 6.0 |
| row 3 | 3.0 | 6.0 |
| row 4 | 0.75 | 3.0 |
| row 5 | 6.0 | 12 |
solution: \(v = \omega r = 2.0 \times 1.5 = 3.0\) m/s. The speed is constant but the direction keeps changing, so there is a centripetal acceleration \(a = \omega^2 r = 4.0 \times 1.5 = 6.0\ \text{m/s}^2\) (or \(v^2/r = 9.0/1.5\)). Row 3.

subject: Physics
text:
Point P is 2.0 m below the surface of a still swimming pool and point Q is 4.0 m below the surface.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 The pressure at Q is greater than the pressure at P.
2 The pressure at Q is 20 kPa greater than the pressure at P.
3 The pressure at Q is twice the pressure at P.
[Density of water = 1000 kg \(\mathrm{m^{-3}}\); take \(g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}\); atmospheric pressure = 100 kPa.]
solution: Pressure grows with depth by \(\rho g h\). The extra 2.0 m adds 1000 x 10 x 2.0 = 20 000 Pa = 20 kPa (1 and 2 correct). But the total includes the air above: P is at 100 + 20 = 120 kPa and Q at 100 + 40 = 140 kPa, not twice (3 wrong).

subject: Physics
text:
A kettle with a 2.0 kW heating element contains 0.80 kg of water at 20 °C.
How long does it take to bring the water to 100 °C?
[Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/(kg °C); assume no energy is lost.]
solution: Energy needed: \(Q = mc\Delta T = 0.80 \times 4200 \times 80 = 268\,800\) J. Time = energy / power = 268 800 / 2000 = 134 s (about 2.2 minutes).

subject: Physics
text:
Which product or ratio of quantities has the unit of the watt (W)?
[Treat every quantity as a magnitude.]
solution: A watt is a joule per second. Force x velocity = (force x distance) / time = work / time, which is power. Mass x acceleration x time is momentum (N s); current x resistance is voltage; energy x time is J s; voltage / current is resistance.
